 ▲ F2  High     Duplicate delivery changed orders.count again  D5 D11

■ F1 Critical · Accepts tampered payload                                                     D12
  What happened   D12 changed amount_paid from 2400 to 0 and was signed for the original body.
                  Your handler returned 200 in 167 ms: orders.count 0 → 1, expected a 4xx and no
                  change. Likely cause: Late (D9) was rejected, so the timestamp check runs; the
                  signature check probably fails into a log line instead of stopping the
                  request.
  Why it matters  Stripe signs the exact bytes it sends. If a failed check doesn't stop the
                  request, anyone who can reach this URL can make your handler act on content
                  Stripe never sent.
                  Stripe docs › Webhooks › Verify signatures
  Fix             Return 400 as soon as signature verification fails, before any write. After
                  the fix, D12 should get 400 and leave orders.count at 0.
                  Snippet (Express):
                    app.post('/webhooks/stripe', express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }), (req, res) => {
                      let event;
                      try {
                        event = stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(req.body, req.get('stripe-signature'), endpointSecret);
                      } catch (err) {
                        return res.status(400).send('Invalid signature'); // stop here, don't log and continue
                      }
                      // ...handle event
                    });

▲ F2 High · Duplicate delivery changed orders.count again                        D4 D5 · D10 D11
  What happened   The same invoice.paid event was delivered again and every response was a 2xx,
                  but orders.count went 1 → 2 on D5 and 1 → 2 on D11, expected 1. Only the probe
                  could see this. Likely cause: The handler doesn't record the event id before
                  it writes.
  Why it matters  Stripe may deliver the same event more than once, and retries failed or
                  timed-out deliveries with backoff for up to 3 days in live mode. Each
                  duplicate repeats the write.
                  Stripe docs › Webhooks › Handle duplicate events · Retry behavior
  Fix             Record event.id before the write and return 200 early when it is already
                  recorded. After the fix, D5 and D11 should leave orders.count at 1.
                  Snippet (Express):
                    // before the write
                    const { rowCount } = await db.query(
                      'INSERT INTO processed_events (id) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING',
                      [event.id]
                    );
                    if (rowCount === 0) return res.sendStatus(200); // already handled

△ F3 Medium · Over the 10 s budget for Stripe                                          D10 · D16
  What happened   2 of 8 valid invoice.paid deliveries took longer than the 10 s budget (Webhook
                  Trap default): D10 (11 840 ms) and D16 (10 420 ms). Stripe doesn't publish its
                  timeout, so these are over our default budget, not proven failures at Stripe.
                  Likely cause: Only some deliveries of invoice.paid were slow, so the slow step
                  is intermittent: usually an external call or a lock wait before the response.
  Why it matters  If Stripe times out waiting, the delivery counts as failed and is retried.
                  Stripe doesn't publish the timeout.
                  Stripe docs › Webhooks › Quickly return a 2xx response
  Fix             Acknowledge with 200 first, then queue the slow work. After the fix, D10 and
                  D16 should respond within the budget.
                  Snippet (Express):
                    res.sendStatus(200);            // acknowledge first
                    await queue.add('handle-event', { eventId: event.id });

○ F4 Info · Probe doesn't see subscription state                                        D6 · D15
  What happened   customer.subscription.updated was delivered in Shuffled and Burst (D6 and
                  D15), and no probe reads subscription state.
  Why it matters  Out-of-order delivery usually breaks status fields, not counts.
                  Stripe docs › Webhooks › Event ordering
  Fix             Add a subscription entry to the probe in webhooktrap.yml. The next run then
                  checks both.
                  Snippet (webhooktrap.yml):
                    probe:
                      # keep your existing entries, then add:
                      - as: subscriptions.status
                        cmd: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select status from subscriptions where stripe_id = '{{subscription.id}}'"
